title: SDK: Tool-call audit transcripts + streaming checksum-backed replay examples (TS/Py/Go)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a cross-language SDK pattern and reference examples that attach tamper-evident audit transcripts to streaming tool/function calls. The goal is to make streaming invocations replayable and searchable in the Console while preserving low-latency incremental delivery. This ticket covers API shape proposals for TypeScript, Python, and Go clients, a compatibility shim for older SDKs (non-streaming fallback), and minimal server-side support needed to store and verify checksummed transcripts for audit and debugging.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by runtime and console owners describing transcript envelope format and checksum algorithm.
TypeScript, Python, and Go examples that demonstrate: attaching per-chunk metadata (seq, timestamp), emitting a final transcript hash, and replaying a transcript end-to-end.
Backward-compatible fallback: non-streaming clients receive a single finalized transcript blob with identical checksum semantics.
Integration README that shows how Console links and search keys are derived from transcript metadata (tool_call_id, model_id, customer_id).
Unit + integration tests for checksum mismatch detection and replay failure modes.
tasks: Draft transcript envelope schema (fields, seq numbers, timestamps, chunk types).
Prototype TS/py/go SDK helpers that wrap streaming generators/async-iterators and emit envelope metadata.
Add server-side minimal verify_and_store endpoint to accept streaming envelopes and produce transcript_id.
Console: prototype UI mock for transcript search and replay; show incremental timestamps and verification status.
Write migration/fallback for legacy clients (single-response transcripts) and document behavior.
